model.meaning: Trust distribution spreads reliance for an outcome across several parties by requiring a threshold of them to act together, so that no single party is decisive, and its real strength is measured by two counts of independent entities, not nominal participants: those needed to reach that threshold and those needed to deny it.

parents.trust-models: Trust Models states that spreading trust reduces reliance on any one party only as far as the parties' failures are independent, and that a large-looking threshold may rest on fewer independent points; Trust Distribution adds how the threshold choice fixes both the coalition that can force an outcome and the absences that can halt it, how the independent count is actually measured (grouping participants by control of keys, stake and infrastructure, counted separately against the forcing and the halting threshold, with the limits of what control is observable), and how that count erodes over time while the nominal count stays the same. It does not restate the parent's independence premise.

claims: the threshold in a distributed trust arrangement: how many parties, or what share of weight, must act together for an outcome, and how that choice sets how many must collude to force a wrong outcome the arrangement accepts on its word and how many must be absent to halt it

measuring how far trust is actually distributed: the smallest number of independent entities able to reach a threshold, counted by control of keys, stake and infrastructure rather than by nominal participants
how distributed trust concentrates over time: stake and delegation gathering in a few operators, signers sharing custody or hosting, and membership that is never renewed

placements.trust-distribution: Under Trust Models the reader has the general account of reliance and the premise that spreading trust helps only with independent failures; the exposition explains thresholds, their measurement and their erosion for any arrangement of signers, validators, committees or reporters, so nothing in it depends on a domain or on a particular protocol.

fields.statement: Trust is distributed for an outcome when the arrangement accepts that outcome only once at least k of n parties, or a share k of total weight such as stake, act for it. The threshold fixes two numbers: the coalition that can force an outcome the arrangement accepts on its word (k), and the parties whose absence or refusal halts it (n - k + 1). How far trust is actually distributed is the smallest number of independent entities whose combined control reaches each of those numbers, which can be far below n.
fields.establishedBy: Choosing the threshold against both failure directions, by what a forced wrong outcome would cost and what a halt would cost and whether a halt has a recovery path; admitting parties whose control of keys, stake and infrastructure is in fact separate; measuring the arrangement by grouping participants under whoever controls their signing keys, their stake (delegated or custodied stake counts under the operator or custodian where that entity, not the owners, decides how the weight is used for the outcome), and their hosting or custody, then counting, over each direction's own grouping and with each member's weight counted once, the fewest groups whose combined control reaches the forcing threshold and, separately, the fewest whose combined control exceeds the total minus the threshold; and repeating the measurement, because the grouping changes over time. Control is often only partly observable (common ownership, off-chain agreements, one owner registered as several participants), so a count from observable groupings is an upper bound on the true number.
fields.violatedBy: Concentration that makes the smallest coalition able to reach a threshold small, whatever the nominal count: stake and delegation gathering in a few operators, through economies of scale, delegators choosing the largest or most familiar operators, and pooled or custodial staking services; signers moving to the same custody provider, signing service or hosting provider for convenience, so that one provider's control or outage reaches many keys at once; and membership that is never renewed, in which members who leave, go inactive, lose keys, merge or hand operations to a common operator are still counted, so the active independent set shrinks while the nominal count does not. Inactive members who are still counted can lower the number of further absences that halt the arrangement without making forcing easier; consolidation can lower both the number that can force it and the number that can halt it.
confusions: nominal participants versus independent entities: n signers or validators under fewer controllers are distributed only across those controllers, and the measure counts controllers
a higher threshold versus a safer arrangement: raising k makes forcing harder and halting easier, so it moves risk from one failure direction to the other rather than removing it
distributing trust versus minimizing it: spreading reliance over many parties leaves the parties collectively trusted; reducing what must be trusted is Trust Minimization, named only

trust distribution versus decentralization: the measure here is taken against a specific trust threshold for a specific outcome, while decentralization is the broader architectural property, named only
a snapshot count versus a lasting one: an arrangement measured as well distributed at launch can concentrate later without any rule changing
fields.tradeoffs: With n parties and threshold k, forcing takes k and halting takes n - k + 1, and the two sum to n + 1: raising k buys resistance to collusion with exposure to halting, and lowering it does the reverse. Adding parties raises both numbers only if the added parties are independent of those already present. Where a halt has a recovery path (a fallback, an exit, re-forming the set), a design can afford a high threshold; where a halt itself causes loss, the halting number weighs as heavily as the forcing one.
fields.relation: Unweighted: force = k, halt = n - k + 1. Weighted with total weight W: forcing needs combined weight of at least k, halting needs absent weight of more than W - k. Measured extent: for each direction, over that direction's grouping of members by controlling entity and with each member's weight counted once, the fewest entities whose combined control reaches k (forcing) or exceeds W - k (halting); where no member falls under two entities, these are the largest entities taken in order of weight. The forcing number counts who can impose a wrong outcome where the outcome is accepted on the threshold's word; where relying parties check the outcome themselves, reaching the forcing number lets a coalition choose only among valid outcomes, and withholding or delaying the outcome takes the halting number. Two conflicting outcomes each reaching threshold need an overlap of 2k - n parties backing both, which belongs to Quorums and is only named.

design.relationship: An arithmetic relation between one threshold choice and two failure numbers, a counting rule with conditions on what counts as independent control and how much of it is observable, and parallel causes by which the count erodes over time.
design.whyProse: The threshold's effect is one relation (k to force, n - k + 1 to halt, summing to n + 1) whose meaning lies in its conditions (outcome accepted on the threshold's word, weighted shares, recovery after a halt), which sentences carry and a comparison of sample thresholds would only tabulate as a formula the paragraph states in a clause. The trade-off is a single pair of forces, which a tensions block with one row would show no better than the sentence that states it. The measurement is a counting rule whose substance is argument: what groups participants (keys, stake, infrastructure), why forcing and halting are counted separately, and why an observed count is an upper bound; the grouping dimensions are variants with one attribute each. The concentration paths are three parallel causes with no order and no return, so neither flow, cycle nor state fits. The nominal-versus-independent conflation is real, but the parent already introduces it, so a distinction block would restate the parent's premise; this concept's addition is how to count, which is explanation.
design.level: Thresholds and their two failure numbers, the independent-entity measure, and erosion over time belong here: Trust Models gives only the premise that spreading trust depends on independence; Trust Assumptions states that an assumption may carry a bound on how many may fail but leaves the threshold choice here; Trusted Parties owns roles and the grounds for trusting each party, not how reliance is split among many; Trust Minimization owns reducing what is trusted.
design.territory: It names collusion, quorums (including the overlap that conflicting outcomes need), fault tolerance, multisignatures, threshold signatures, Byzantine behavior, decentralization and trust minimization without explaining them: the threshold is treated as a reliance arrangement, not as a signature scheme or consensus rule; collusion is the act the forcing number counts, not explained; the measure is framed against a trust threshold, not as decentralization in general. It does not restate the parent's paragraph on independent failures, nor Trust Assumptions' anatomy of a bound or Trusted Parties' grounds for trust such as stake at risk.
design.placements: The concept has one placement, under Trust Models; the exposition is general to any arrangement that requires several parties to act, uses no positional references, and its examples, where used, should be drawn from more than one setting (validators, signer sets, committees, reporters) so that it does not imply a single protocol.

audit.note: Re-audit after repair 2, fresh context; every sentence of the 6-paragraph prose record (about 1,130 words) read against criteria 1-6. Prior findings resolved: trust-distribution.md D1-D6 and trust-distribution-b.md D1-D4 stay resolved (conditional delegated-stake grouping; host with only take-offline power groups for halting, steering host for both; per-direction grouping, each member counted once, fewest groups, largest-first conditioned on disjoint groups; forcing coalition chooses only among passing outcomes, withholding/delaying takes the halting number; pooled staking 'can bring ... one operator's keys or a few'; definition names two counts; consolidation 'can lower'). trust-distribution-2.md E1 resolved: 'Where every member other than the colluders approves no wrong outcome and alone controls its keys, k is how many must collude to force a wrong one; stolen keys or members misled into approving lower that number' - the condition now excludes misled approvers and stolen keys (so the listed exceptions break it rather than contradict it), it is sufficient (every approval of a wrong outcome must come from a colluder), and the count is restricted to a wrong outcome, matching claim 1. Repair remarks applied: paragraph 5 'each count is taken against one threshold for one outcome'; paragraph 6 'A member that no longer takes part but is still counted among the n is already absent, so it can reduce the further absences needed to halt the outcome without making forcing easier'; model violatedBy aligned ('can lower'). Narrowed terms re-read in untouched sentences: 'wrong' (P2 'wrong or not', P3 'counts who can impose a wrong outcome only where ... accepted on the threshold's word', 'cost of a forced wrong outcome') is one sense, an outcome that should not be accepted; 'collude' (P3 'a threshold chosen only against collusion') named only; 'count' is used as noun for the two measured counts and generically ('a count built from observed links ... never raise it' holds since merging or overlapping groups cannot raise a minimum, given real observed links) and as the verb 'count alike'/'counted among the n', no conflicting sense; 'n' is the nominal total throughout (P2 arithmetic, P4 'far smaller than n', P6 'still counted among the n'); 'absent' covers outage, lost key, refusal and inactivity, consistent between P2 and P6. Arithmetic: k and n - k + 1 sum to n + 1; ends of range; weighted forcing reaches the threshold, halting needs absent weight above total minus threshold; halting count 'exceeds the total minus the threshold' matches n - k + 1 unweighted. Parent overlap: none; the Trust Models independence paragraph is built on (how to count, by direction, over time), not restated; the domain sentence on bounds of faulty or colluding parties is not restated. Territory: Collusion, Quorums, Decentralization and Trust Minimization named only; fault tolerance, multisignatures, threshold signatures and Byzantine behavior not explained; Trusted Parties' discretion appears only as a clause bounding the forcing number; Trust Minimization boundary is a mirrored naming sentence, acceptable. All three claims explained. Representation: prose as designed; design reasoning holds. One placement (Foundations / Trust Models); no positional or time-sensitive words; American English; plain text. Depth follows the three claims; no point made twice. Remarks: (R1) the custodian/signing-service clause groups members for halting only where members depend on that party to sign (true of the roles as Trusted Parties defines them, not of an escrow holding a copy); (R2) definition's 'a threshold amount of their combined weight ... act for it' has weight as the subject of act; (R3) 'without making forcing easier' assumes the threshold is fixed over total membership, which the record's model is; (R4) 'can only overstate' would read more exactly as 'can only overstate or match'; (R5) model claim 1 and fields.statement still say 'share k of total weight' while the record says an amount often set as a share, and fields.statement's 'the smallest number ... that reaches each of those numbers' is singular-ish; the record is right.

resolutions.resolution: Collusion is named only: 'k is how many must collude to force a wrong one' (the act the forcing number counts, per the design's territory) and 'a threshold chosen only against collusion'. How collusion works or is prevented is not explained.

Decentralization is named only, to say the per-outcome, per-threshold measure is narrower ('which keeps the measure narrower than Decentralization'); the reason given is this concept's own (each count against one threshold for one outcome), and decentralization is not described.

Quorums is named to assign whether two conflicting outcomes could each gather the threshold, which 'turns on how far the sets backing them must overlap'; no overlap arithmetic (2k - n) or intersection argument is given. Reference, not explanation.

Trust Minimization is named only: 'reducing what has to be trusted at all is Trust Minimization', drawing the boundary that a high count leaves the parties trusted collectively; its means, assumption and costs are not explained. The mirrored sentence in the Trust Minimization record names Trust Distribution back.

Each holds: 'cannot or will not' describes members that do not act; 'not always in both directions' is a hedge; 'never raise it' holds because hidden links can only merge groups or add overlap, which cannot raise a minimum, under the stated proviso that observed links are real; 'never renewed' is the condition of claim 3, with 'can decay'. Other absolutes read: 'every member other than the colluders approves no wrong outcome' is the stated condition; 'any member can force/halt' holds at thresholds of one and n; 'only' uses (choose only among outcomes that pass, only where accepted on the threshold's word, only power is to take offline, only partly observable, only at the time taken, chosen only against collusion) are each accurate as conditioned.

groupAudit.note: Group audit of trust-models (six owned members read side by side with the parent Trust Models). group-signals prints 0 signals, so there are no resolutions; drift reports nothing for the group. Flagged sentence judged: Trust Distribution's 'A high count also still leaves the parties trusted collectively for whatever the threshold accepts on their word; reducing what has to be trusted at all is Trust Minimization.' and Trust Minimization's 'Many operators can still be trusted collectively: a committee whose attestations are accepted on its word ... a matter for Trust Distribution, and adding members does not make its outputs checked.' are reciprocal boundary sentences, not one argument made twice: each names the other concept to mark its edge and neither explains the other's mechanism (TD does not describe any means of minimization; TM leaves how many must fail together to TD). They serve different claims (TD: what its measured count does not establish; TM: the Trust Minimization / Decentralization distinction), agree with each other and with the parent, and the shared phrasing ('trusted collectively', 'on its/their word') is a one-clause echo, acceptable but worth varying if TD is ever reopened. Cross-member checks: references between members (thresholds to TD, one-honest-participant to TM, discretion to Trusted Parties, checks to Verification, collusion and quorums out of group) are boundary references only and consistent; no contradictions found (signers attesting to unchecked statements in TP/TD, the one-honest-peer reliance in TB/TM, challenge-window failure in TA/Verification/TM each taken from a different angle). Upgrade authority recurs in TA, TP, TB and TM, each under its own claim (an implicit assumption that can change other assumptions; a key-holder role; a moved boundary with new crossings; an authority that can undo minimization means), not one argument repeated. Narrowing discretion (TP, cost of responsiveness) and removing overrides (TM, cost of intervention) are distinct costs. 'Bound' carries three qualified senses across members (TA's bound on failures, TM's bounding a party's powers, Verification's error bound), each clear in context and none within one record. Convergence: definitional openings are the contract's lead; the enumerations (TA four parts, Verification three parts and three roles, TM four means and three needs) are the counts the plan's claims name, so repetition follows the claims; forms differ (TA, TP, TB, TD prose only at different lengths; Verification and TM each one comparison where alternatives vary along dimensions; TM's one distinction answers a real conflation), with no shared arc or paragraph template.
